fact_text: A foreign national sponsored for an Indian Employment (E) Visa in any sector must draw a salary in excess of US$ 25,000 per annum; the application may be rejected if this minimum annual income benchmark is not met.
evidence_quote: should draw a salary in excess of US$ 25,000 per annum.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any Indian job offer qualifies a foreigner for a work visa. Actually the Employment Visa carries a hard salary floor of over US$ 25,000/year across all sectors. Action: confirm the total package clears US$ 25,000 before filing.

entity_title: E-Visa not for jobs Indians can fill
fact_text: An Indian Employment Visa is not granted for jobs for which qualified Indians are available, nor for routine, ordinary or secretarial/clerical roles - it is reserved for highly skilled or qualified professionals.
evidence_quote: Employment Visa shall not be granted for jobs for which qualified Indians are available. Employment Visa shall also not be granted for routine, ordinary or secretarial/clerical jobs.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed an employer can sponsor any hire onto a work visa. Actually the role must genuinely require a foreign professional; clerical/secretarial or Indian-fillable roles are refused. Action: document why the position needs this specific skilled foreign national.

fact_text: The Indian Employment Visa is tied to a single sponsoring employer: the name of the sponsoring employer/organization is printed on the visa sticker itself.
evidence_quote: The name of the sponsoring employer / organization shall be clearly stipulated in the visa sticker.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work visa lets you change jobs freely once in India. Actually the visa names your sponsoring employer on the sticker and is bound to it. Action: treat any employer change as requiring a fresh visa authorisation, not just a new contract.

fact_text: A Business (B) Visa does not authorise working in India: its conditions expressly exclude visiting India for full-time employment. Taking up a job requires the Employment (E) Visa.
evidence_quote: The foreign national should not be visiting India for the business of money lending or for running a petty business or petty trade or for full time employment in India, etc.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can start work on a business visa while the work visa is arranged. Actually a Business Visa explicitly bars full-time employment in India. Action: do not begin employment until the Employment Visa is issued.

fact_text: If an Employment Visa is valid for more than 180 days, the holder must register with the FRRO/FRO (via e-FRRO) within 14 days of arrival in India.
evidence_quote: the E-visa holder must register with the FRRO/FRO concerned within 14 days of arrival.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed registration is only for very long stays or is optional. Actually any E-visa valid over 180 days triggers a 14-day FRRO registration clock from the date of arrival. Action: complete the e-FRRO registration within the first two weeks.

entity_title: No FRRO registration if visa 180 days or less
fact_text: An Employment Visa issued for 180 days or less does not require registration with the FRRO/FRO - the trigger is the visa's validity period, not the length of the trip.
evidence_quote: In the case of Employment Visa issued for a period of 180 days or less, registration is not required with FRRO/FRO.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed every foreign worker must register with the authorities. Actually a short E-visa valid for 180 days or less is exempt from FRRO registration. Action: read your visa's validity endorsement to know whether registration applies.

entity_title: Report change of address to FRRO
fact_text: After registering, any change in the foreign national's residential address in India must be reported in writing to the FRRO/FRO immediately.
evidence_quote: if there is any change in the residential address, the foreign national concerned shall immediately report the change of address, in writing, to the FRRO/FRO concerned.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you deal with the FRRO only once, at arrival. Actually every later change of home address must be reported to the FRRO in writing. Action: notify the FRRO whenever you move house within India.

fact_text: Year-to-year extension of an Employment Visa (up to a total of 5 years) is granted only subject to conditions that include the filing of Indian Income Tax returns.
evidence_quote: subject to good conduct, production of necessary documents in support of continued employment, filing of Income Tax returns and no adverse security inputs about the foreigner.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a visa extension is a routine paperwork stamp. Actually extensions are conditioned on having filed Indian Income Tax returns. Action: keep your Indian tax filings current so the visa can be extended.

entity_title: E-Visa must be obtained before arrival
fact_text: An Employment Visa must be issued from the applicant's country of origin, or country of domicile where they have been a permanent resident for more than 2 years - it cannot be obtained by converting another visa after entering India.
evidence_quote: The Employment Visa must be issued from the country of origin or from the country of domicile of the foreigner

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can enter on a tourist/business visa and switch to a work visa inside India. Actually the Employment Visa must be granted from your home or domicile country beforehand. Action: apply at the Indian mission abroad before relocating.

fact_text: For Indian income tax, a relocating professional becomes tax-resident if present in India for 182 days or more in the tax year (or 60 days in the year plus 365 days across the preceding four years).
evidence_quote: he stays in India for 182 days or more in the relevant tax year, or for 60 days or more in that year coupled with 365 days or more in the preceding four years.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you remain a non-resident for tax as long as you hold a foreign passport. Actually 182 days in India in a tax year makes you an Indian tax resident under Section 6. Action: track your day-count from the date of arrival.

fact_text: A newly-arrived foreign professional is usually classified 'Not Ordinarily Resident' (RNOR): an individual is not ordinarily resident in a tax year if he was non-resident in nine out of ten preceding years, or stayed in India for 729 days or less in the preceding seven years.
evidence_quote: in nine out of ten preceding years or stayed in India for 729 days or less in the preceding seven years.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed that becoming an Indian tax resident means India taxes your worldwide income from day one. Actually the Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR) sub-status generally keeps foreign-source income outside the Indian net in the early years. Action: check your RNOR eligibility before your first Indian tax filing.
